_readme: Per-locale App Store subtitle + keywords. STAGED ONLY — a human submits.
The app NAME never changes and is never written: it stays 'Earth Around: Space Weather' and a
new localization inherits it. That has a consequence this file exists to answer — the heaviest
field is frozen in English, so in every other language the localized HEAD NOUN has to come from
the subtitle and the keywords, spelled out in full. Each locale therefore carries a complete
phrase set on its own; keywords never combine across locales.
Head nouns were verified against each language's own authority rather than translated:
de  DLR uses Polarlicht / geomagnetischer Sturm; 'Sonnensturm' is the popular search form
fr  OQLF + Termium approve 'tempête géomagnétique'; 'orage magnétique' is the older form
es  media and general readers say 'llamarada'/'erupción'; 'fulguración' is research register
ja  NICT uses 磁気嵐 and デリンジャー現象/短波通信障害; オーロラ予報 is the searched phrase
Rules applied (marketing/autoaso.md §6/§6.5): no word repeated between subtitle and keywords,
no 'app', no category name, no plural of an included singular, no space after a comma.
2026-08-03 — SUBTITLE REBUILT AROUND THE MEASURED PHRASE.
US autocomplete (storefront 143441-1,29) measured on 2026-08-03:
aurora forecast   10 hits, incl. 'aurora forecast apps' — shopping intent, strongest signal
aurora alert      10   aurora borealis 5   space weather 8   kp index 3   solar flare 3
solar storm        0 — DEAD. It had been holding 11 of the 27 subtitle characters.
geomagnetic storm  2, both of them app names: supply, not demand
northern lights / aurora (bare): polluted — pizza, credit union, VPN, health care
So 'aurora forecast' moves to subtitle weight and 'solar storm' is gone; 'kp' and 'forecast'
leave the keyword field because a term in two fields is indexed once and paid for twice.
ONLY ENGLISH IS MEASURED. Apple's hints endpoint needs a per-market storefront ID and none are
recorded here, so the other 18 locales mirror the English STRUCTURE — forecast phrase in the
subtitle, Kp with it, dead storm-word dropped — without evidence that their local terms rank the
same way. 'Sonnensturm' being dead in the US says nothing about German demand. Measure per
storefront before treating any non-English line as validated.
